question:
Opponent shuffling your deck.
Last weekend I went to a Modern qualifier, and, at the first match, I faced a guy who kept shuffling my deck twice every single time.
Before the game started, I shuffled the deck around 20 times.
Then, at each fetching, tutor, or else, I usually shuffle the deck 7 times (because I read that's a fair number to randomize the deck).
I always mash shuffle by making sure the card on top is never the same and always shuffle in front of my opponent, so no attempt to kind of manipulate the deck in a way they can't see it.
Also, I was playing Lantern Control and often had a lantern in play, so any topdeck manipulation would have been OBVIOUS in some game spots.
The guy always took my deck and shuffled it twice while I was just chill and kept cutting his deck into 2 or 3 parts.
I have to admit that it was annoying to the point I almost thought of asking him to shuffle my deck instead of me. Why waste time and energy when he can do the work for me?
I even thought of starting to shuffle his deck a ridiculous number of times just to meta-tell him that it was annoying.
I was so stunned that I asked a couple of friends there, and they were like, "that went too far".
I don't know if it's legal to shuffle the opponent's deck every s i n g l e time, but I guess it might be.
Is it among my rights to ask just to cut it?
However, that seemed to me quite a passive-aggressive approach.
I might sound rude, but I've never been in such an annoying situation. I only faced people who shuffled my deck at the very beginning of the game.
reference:
What REL was the tournament being held at?
From the Magic Tournament Rules:
3.10 Card Shuffling
Decks must be randomized at the start of every game and whenever an instruction requires it. Randomization is defined as bringing the deck to a state where no player can have any information regarding the order or position of cards in any portion of the deck. Pile shuffling may not be performed other than once each at the beginning of a game to count the cards in the deck.
Once the deck is randomized, it must be presented to an opponent. By this action, players state that their decks are legal and randomized. The opponent may then shuffle it additionally. Cards and sleeves must not be in danger of being damaged during this process. If the opponent does not believe the player made a reasonable effort to randomize their deck, the opponent must notify a judge. Players may request to have a judge shuffle their cards rather than the opponent; this request will be honored only at a judge’s discretion.
If a player has had the opportunity to see any of the card faces of the deck being shuffled, the deck is no longer considered randomized and must be randomized again.
At Competitive and Professional Rules Enforcement Level tournaments, players are required to shuffle their opponents’ decks after their owners have shuffled them. The Head Judge can require this at Regular Rules Enforcement Level tournaments as well.
Your opponent has the right to shuffle after you do, every single time, and actually is required to at Competitive, which might be the REL for the event.
Also, I was playing Lantern Control and often had a lantern in play, so any topdeck manipulation would have been OBVIOUS in some game spots.
For experienced cardists, it's trivial to shuffle a certain card to the second or third from top, so it wouldn't have been obvious.
